FOR THE RESPONDENT : In person 

 

 

 

 

 

 

: O R D E R :
HONBLE JUSTICE
SRI KALIDAS MUKHERJEE, PRESIDENT 

 

 

 

 This
appeal is directed against the judgment and order passed by Learned District
Forum, Siliguri in case no.7/S/2011 allowing the complaint and directing the OP
to pay the sum of Rs.20,000/- together with the interest @ 10% per annum from
15/04/10 and to credit the said sum to the SB A/c of the complainant within 45
days from the date of order failing which the amount will carry interest @ 9%
per annum till realization. The OP was
further directed to pay the compensation of Rs.2,000/- within 45 days failing
which the amount will carry interest @ 9% per annum from the date of the
institution of the case till realization.
The
case of the complainant/respondent, in short, is that he has a savings bank
account bearing no.11089313861 with the OP bank and got the ATM Card from the
OP. On 15/04/10 he went to the ATM
Counter situated at Deshbandhu Para, Siliguri to withdraw money at 8.15
a.m. The complainant inserted his ATM
Card and some formalities were displayed on the screen of the ATM Machine and
he completed the procedure except the putting of PIN Number. Thereafter the machine did not function. The complainant several times tried to cancel
the displayed screen, but it did not come back to the normal screen and the
complainant being frustrated left the place.
On 15/04/10 the complainant left Siliguri and went to Champa within the
State of Chattisgarh. On 21/04/10 he went to the ATM Counter at
Railway Station at Champa to withdraw the sum of Rs.2,000/-. He found that the sum of Rs.20,000/- was
missing from his SB A/c. On 01/05/10 he
went to ATM Counter at Kalyan in the State of Maharashtra where he found from the Mini
Statement that the sum of Rs.20,000/- was withdrawn on 15/04/10. He had registered on line complaint on
11/05/10. He lodged a complaint with the
OP to produce and deliver a computerized ATM list so that he could see the time
of transaction in question. On 26/05/10
he had lodged complaint with the Siliguri P.S.
and the GD Entry No.2427 dated26/05/10 was recorded. It has been alleged that the PIN number of
the ATM Card was unauthorisedly taken away and the complainant was deprived of
due service. It was deficiency in
service on the part of the OP. For the
said reasons, the complaint was instituted before the Learned District Forum.
The
Learned Counsel for the appellant has submitted that in the complaint it has
been alleged that he could not put the PIN number on 15/04/10, but the ATM/JP
Log shows that the transaction was complete and the sum of Rs.20,000/- was
withdrawn. It is contended that the
allegation as raised in Para 12 of the
complaint that the PIN number was unauthorisedly taken away cannot be believed
at all.
The respondent/complainant, in person, has submitted that
the CCTV footage was not produced by the bank.
It is contended that there was deficiency in service on the part of the
OP bank.
We
have heard the submission made by both sides and perused the materials on
record. It has been contended by the
respondent/complainant as per averment made in the complaint that on 15/04/10
he went to the ATM Counter at Siliguri to withdraw money and after inserting
the ATM Card he followed the procedure except the putting of the PIN
number. In other words, it is the
contention of the complainant that it was an abortive attempt on his part to
withdraw money as the transaction failed.
But the OP bank has filed ATM/JP Log from which it would appear that on
15/04/10 at 8.04 a.m. the sum of Rs.20,000/- was withdrawn. It is quite clear that unless the ATM Card is
inserted into the ATM Machine followed by the putting of PIN number, there
would not be any successful transaction.
In this connection the contention of the complainant as made in Para 12 of the complaint is that the PIN number of his
ATM Card was unauthorisedly taken away.
It has not been stated therein by whom it was taken away. Not only that there is no averment as to
whether or not the complainant lodged any GD regarding the unauthorized taking
away of PIN number of his ATM Card.
There is nothing to show that the complainant informed the bank seeking
cancellation of the ATM Card on the ground that its PIN number was
unauthorisedly taking away by somebody.
The contention of the complainant in this regard is not acceptable. There is nothing to disbelieve the statement
as per ATM/JP Log. Under the
circumstances, we are of the considered view that the complainant is not
entitled to get any relief and the Learned District Forum was not justified in
allowing the complaint.
In
the result, the appeal succeeds and the same stands allowed. We set aside the impugned judgment and
order. The petition of complaint is
dismissed. We make no order as to costs.
MEMBER(L) PRESIDENT
